about.title: About Minimum Payment Calculator - Credit Card Payoff Timeline Tool
about.description: The Minimum Payment Calculator is a comprehensive debt analysis tool designed to help you understand how long it takes to pay off credit card debt using only minimum payments and the total interest costs involved. This calculator shows the true cost of making minimum payments, helping you make informed decisions about debt repayment strategies. Whether you're managing existing debt or planning payment strategies, this tool provides eye-opening analysis of minimum payment consequences.

faq.q: Why do minimum payments take so long to pay off debt?
faq.a: Minimum payments are typically 2-3% of the balance, with most going toward interest rather than principal. As the balance decreases, so does the minimum payment, extending payoff time significantly.

faq.q: How much interest will I pay with minimum payments?
faq.a: With minimum payments, total interest often equals or exceeds the original balance. For example, a $5,000 balance at 18% APR with 2% minimum payments takes 30+ years and costs over $6,000 in interest.

faq.q: What's better than making minimum payments?
faq.a: Pay a fixed amount above the minimum, focus extra payments on highest-rate cards first (debt avalanche), or consider debt consolidation at lower rates. Even $25-50 extra monthly can cut years off payoff time.

faq.q: Should I pay more than the minimum on all cards?
faq.a: Pay minimums on all cards to avoid late fees, then put any extra money toward the highest interest rate card first. This 'debt avalanche' method minimizes total interest costs.
